facts.text: Rutherford was founded on the nearly 12,000‑acre Mexican land grant Rancho Caymus, given to early settler George C. Yount.
In 1864, Yount gifted a 1,040‑acre parcel to his granddaughter Elizabeth and her husband Thomas Rutherford, a wedding present that seeded the town’s wine legacy.
The town’s name honors Thomas Rutherford, whose family planted vineyards in the late 1800s, laying the groundwork for Rutherford AVA.
Rutherford hosts the historic Inglenook estate, bought by filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola in 1975, which now houses a museum on wine and cinema history.
The Auberge du Soleil resort and restaurant sit within Rutherford, offering guests a taste of the region’s renowned terroir.
Rutherford’s soil, once a riverbed, gives its wines a depth of flavor with fruit notes and subtle herbaceous undertones that linger after the last sip.
